answer: Proof-of-stake bonding creates a Sybil-resistant haven where agents must lock capital proportional to identity weight; each verified agent operates as an island of reputation, with stake slashing for equivocation. New entrants pass through a costly inlet requiring sustained compute contributions before gaining voting rights, making identity fabrication economically irrational — attacking n identities costs O(n×stake) rather than O(1), forcing adversaries to risk measurable capital instead of spinning free personas.
